mail.extension.name: Mail
mail.extension.description: MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MTA-STS and TLS reporting.
mail.no_inbound: The domain receives no mail: this check does not apply.
mail.mx.title: Mail servers
mail.mx.why: MX records say where the domain's mail arrives. This is information, unless a server named there cannot be reached.
mail.mx.none: No mail server: the domain receives no mail.
mail.mx.null_mixed: A "0 ." MX record (domain without mail) sits next to real servers: the standard forbids it and senders may refuse to write to the domain.
mail.mx.null_mixed.how: If the domain receives mail, delete the "0 ." MX record. If it does not, delete the others.
mail.mx.address: An MX record gives an IP address ({hosts}) instead of a server name: senders ignore it.
mail.mx.address.how: An MX must name a host (mx.example.com) that has an address itself. Create that name, then point the MX to it.
mail.mx.unresolved: {n:mail server has|mail servers have} no address in the DNS ({hosts}): mail meant for them cannot be delivered.
mail.mx.message:
Hello,

The MX record of {domain} names servers without an address in the DNS ({hosts}): mail meant for them cannot be delivered.

Could you check the MX records?

Thank you.
mail.spf.title: Allowed senders (SPF)
mail.spf.action: Publish the list of allowed senders (SPF)
mail.spf.why: SPF publishes the list of servers allowed to send e-mail for the domain. Receiving mail services use it to set fakes aside.
mail.spf.ref: RFC 7208 · ANSSI, « Recommandations pour la mise en place d'une passerelle d'interconnexion sécurisée »
mail.spf.missing: No SPF record: nothing says who may send e-mail for the domain.
mail.spf.how: The proposed value is a starting point. If other services send e-mail on your behalf (newsletter, invoicing software, website), add their "include": each one gives it in its help pages.
mail.spf.multiple: Several SPF records: receiving services ignore all of them.
mail.spf.multiple.how: A domain must have a single SPF record. Gather their mechanisms (include, ip4…) into one, then delete the others.
mail.spf.too_many_lookups: The SPF record needs {count} DNS lookups, beyond the limit of {limit}: it fails for every recipient.
mail.spf.lookups.message:
Hello,

The SPF record of {domain} needs {count} DNS lookups, while the standard (RFC 7208) allows {limit}. Beyond that, recipients treat the SPF check as failed.

Could you simplify it, for instance by removing services that no longer send e-mail for us?

Thank you.
mail.spf.pass_all: The SPF record ends with "+all": it allows the whole world to send on your behalf.
mail.spf.pass_all.action: Fix the end of the SPF record
mail.spf.pass_all.how: Replace "+all" (or a bare "all") with "~all", then with "-all" once you are sure the list of senders is complete.
mail.spf.neutral: The SPF record ends with "?all": mail sent from elsewhere is not flagged.
mail.spf.neutral.action: Tighten the end of the SPF record
mail.spf.neutral.how: End the record with "~all" (other senders are suspicious) or "-all" (they are refused).
mail.spf.no_all: The SPF record does not say what to do with other senders.
mail.spf.ok: An SPF record lists the allowed senders and ends with "{policy}".
mail.spf.syntax: The SPF record holds an invalid term ({terms}): receivers reject it as a whole (permanent error).
mail.spf.syntax.how: Each term must be a known mechanism (ip4:, ip6:, a, mx, include:, exists:, all) or a modifier (redirect=, exp=). Check the spelling and the addresses of the term reported.
mail.spf.broken_include: The SPF record points to {targets}, which does not have exactly one valid SPF record: the check ends in an error at receivers.
mail.spf.broken_include.how: Remove the "include" or "redirect" to that name if it is no longer used, or ask the service concerned for the exact name to include.
mail.spf.ptr: The SPF record uses the "ptr" mechanism, which the standard advises against: it is slow and some receivers ignore it.
mail.spf.ptr.how: Replace "ptr" by the addresses (ip4:, ip6:) or names (a:) of the servers that send the mail.
mail.dmarc.title: Protection against spoofing (DMARC)
mail.dmarc.why: Without DMARC, anyone can send an e-mail that seems to come from the domain, such as a fake invoice with other bank details. DMARC tells mail services what to do with such fakes, and sends you reports.
mail.dmarc.ref: RFC 9989 (replaces RFC 7489) · ANSSI, « Recommandations pour la mise en place d'une passerelle d'interconnexion sécurisée »
mail.dmarc.missing: No DMARC policy: anyone can send e-mail in the domain's name.
mail.dmarc.how: Safe: with p=none no e-mail is blocked, you only get reports at the address given. That mailbox must exist, work and be read: create it, or replace it with an address you already read. Once the reports are clean, move to p=quarantine.
mail.dmarc.multiple: Several DMARC policies on {name}: receiving services ignore all of them.
mail.dmarc.multiple_inherited: Multiple DMARC policies at {name} are ignored; the policy at {parent} (p={policy}) applies. Remove the local duplicates.
mail.dmarc.multiple.how: Delete the extra _dmarc records so that only one is left.
mail.dmarc.monitoring: DMARC is in monitoring mode (p=none): fake e-mails are still delivered.
mail.dmarc.monitoring.how: Before publishing this record: check that the DMARC reports do reach the address given and that someone reads them (if it is on another domain, that domain must allow the reports with a _report._dmarc record); then check in those reports that your real e-mail (mailbox, newsletter, invoicing) passes. Only then do fakes go to the recipients' spam folder. The record offered keeps neither t=y nor pct: with them, the quarantine would not apply to every failing e-mail. Without an sp value, the quarantine also applies to the subdomains: check their mail in the reports too. An sp or np value already there is kept as written.
mail.dmarc.invalid: The DMARC policy of {name} cannot be read: unknown policy value ({tags}).
mail.dmarc.partial: At receivers that still follow RFC 7489, only {pct}% of the e-mails failing DMARC are selected for quarantine ("pct" tag); the others go through their usual filtering.
mail.dmarc.partial.how: The "pct" tag comes from RFC 7489; RFC 9989 made it historic and no longer uses it. Receivers that still follow RFC 7489 apply the policy to the share given only: with p=reject, the other failing e-mails should be quarantined; with p=quarantine, they go through the usual filtering. Remove "pct" from the _dmarc record. For a gradual roll-out, "t=y" is the RFC 9989 mechanism, but older receivers ignore it and apply the declared policy.
mail.dmarc.enforced: The DMARC policy (p={policy}) sets fake e-mails aside.
mail.dmarc.malformed: A {name} record exists but does not start with "v=DMARC1": receiving services ignore it, the domain is not protected.
mail.dmarc.malformed.how: The record must start exactly with "v=DMARC1;" followed by "p=…". For instance: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@{domain}
mail.dmarc.monitoring_inherited: The domain follows the DMARC policy of {parent}, which is in monitoring mode: fake e-mails are still delivered.
mail.dmarc.monitoring_inherited.action: Publish a DMARC policy of the domain's own
mail.dmarc.monitoring_inherited.how: The policy applied is the one of {parent}, which you may not manage. Publish a policy of this domain's own: first p=none with a report address that exists and that you read, then p=quarantine once the reports show that your real e-mail passes. If {parent} is a public suffix (such as gouv.fr), receivers that still follow RFC 7489 apply no policy at all to this domain until it has its own.
mail.dmarc.syntax: The DMARC policy (p={policy}) contains invalid values: {tags}. How they are handled may depend on the error and the receiving mail service; the record should be corrected.
mail.dmarc.syntax.action: Fix the values of the DMARC policy
mail.dmarc.syntax.how: Accepted values: pct from 0 to 100, adkim and aspf r or s, rua and ruf "mailto:address@domain" addresses separated by commas. Remove or fix the tags reported in {name}.
mail.dmarc.subdomains_open: The DMARC policy (p={policy}) leaves the subdomains out (sp=none): a fake e-mail from invoices.{domain} would be delivered.
mail.dmarc.subdomains_open.how: Remove "sp=none" from the _dmarc record so that subdomains follow the same policy, or set sp=quarantine.
mail.dmarc.enforced_inherited: The domain is protected by the DMARC policy of {parent} (p={policy} for subdomains).
mail.dkim.title: E-mail signature (DKIM)
mail.dkim.why: DKIM lets recipients verify email signatures. This check inspects public keys in DNS, not actual outgoing messages.
mail.dkim.not_found: No DKIM key found under the usual names. It may exist under another one: your mail service will tell you.
mail.dkim.weak_key: DKIM key of {bits} bits ({selectors}): too short to be safe.
mail.dkim.short_key: DKIM key of {bits} bits ({selectors}): 2048 bits are recommended.
mail.dkim.message:
Hello,

The published DKIM public key for {domain} is only {bits} bits long (selector {selectors}). Current recommendations call for 2048-bit RSA keys.

Could you generate a new 2048-bit RSA key and provide the DNS record to publish, after checking with your mail service configuration?

Thank you.
mail.dkim.found: A valid DKIM public key is published (selector: {selectors}). Actual outgoing email signatures were not verified.
mail.dkim.unreadable: A published DKIM key cannot be read ({selectors}): e-mails signed with it fail verification.
mail.dkim.unreadable.message:
Hello,

The DKIM key published for {domain} (selector {selectors}) cannot be read: it is probably cut or copied wrongly. E-mails signed with this key fail verification.

Could you send us the exact DNS record to publish again?

Thank you.
mail.mta_sts.title: Encryption required on delivery (MTA-STS)
mail.mta_sts.why: MTA-STS makes the servers that write to you encrypt the connection and check they talk to the right server. Without it, someone in between can read or divert the mail.
mail.mta_sts.message:
Hello,

Could you set up MTA-STS (RFC 8461) for {domain}? It needs a _mta-sts record and a policy file at https://mta-sts.{domain}/.well-known/mta-sts.txt, first in "testing" mode, then "enforce".

Thank you.
mail.mta_sts.no_policy: The MTA-STS record exists but the policy file cannot be found.
mail.mta_sts.testing: MTA-STS is in "{mode}" mode: encryption is not required yet.
mail.mta_sts.testing.action: Verify MX TLS readiness before switching MTA-STS to "enforce"
mail.mta_sts.enforce_message:
Hello,

The MTA-STS policy of {domain} is in "testing" mode. Before enabling "enforce", please verify STARTTLS negotiation, MX certificate trust and hostname matching, MX policy coverage and TLS-RPT reports over a representative period. Missing reports or DNS checks alone do not prove the change is safe.

Thank you.
mail.mta_sts.enforce: An MTA-STS policy in enforce mode is published and covers the announced MX; STARTTLS availability and SMTP certificates are evaluated separately.
mail.mta_sts.bad_record: The _mta-sts record is invalid or duplicated (there must be a single "v=STSv1; id=…"): senders ignore MTA-STS.
mail.mta_sts.bad_certificate: The MTA-STS policy file is served with a certificate that is not trusted ({problem}): senders ignore it.
mail.mta_sts.bad_policy: The MTA-STS policy file is incomplete or invalid (fields: {fields}): senders ignore it.
mail.mta_sts.disabled: MTA-STS is published in "none" mode: it protects nothing.
mail.mta_sts.mx_mismatch: The MTA-STS policy (mode {mode}) does not cover {n:mail server|mail servers} ({hosts}). In "enforce" mode, senders refuse to deliver mail to them.
mail.mta_sts.mx_mismatch.action: Add the mail servers to the MTA-STS policy
mail.mta_sts.mx_message:
Hello,

The MTA-STS policy of {domain} (https://mta-sts.{domain}/.well-known/mta-sts.txt) does not mention these mail servers: {hosts}. Could you add an "mx:" line for each, then change the id of the _mta-sts record?

Thank you.
mail.mta_sts.short_max_age: The MTA-STS policy is only remembered for {seconds:second|seconds}: the protection lasts little between two visits.
mail.mta_sts.max_age_message:
Hello,

The MTA-STS policy of {domain} has a duration (max_age) of {seconds} seconds. The standard recommends several weeks, for instance max_age: 1209600. Could you lengthen it?

Thank you.
mail.smtp_starttls.title: SMTP encryption of the receiving servers (STARTTLS)
mail.smtp_starttls.action: Have the mail servers offer STARTTLS and a valid certificate
mail.smtp_starttls.why: The servers that write to you encrypt the connection with STARTTLS on port 25. Without STARTTLS, or without a certificate valid for the server's name, mail can travel in clear or be diverted, and MTA-STS cannot be enforced.
mail.smtp_starttls.probe_off: SMTP check not run: the probe is turned off on this instance. The MTA-STS results do not include the check of STARTTLS on port 25.
mail.smtp_starttls.internal: SMTP check not run in an internal perimeter: it only concerns public servers.
mail.smtp_starttls.ok: Every published address of the mail servers offers STARTTLS and presents a certificate valid for the server's name. Tested from this instance.
mail.smtp_starttls.ok_partial: STARTTLS and a valid certificate were verified on at least one address of each mail server, but the measure is incomplete (see the notes). Do not switch to enforce on the basis of this result alone.
mail.smtp_starttls.starttls_absent: The server {host} does not offer STARTTLS in its EHLO reply. This was observed on the address {address}.
mail.smtp_starttls.starttls_absent.actio: Turn on STARTTLS on the mail servers
mail.smtp_starttls.certificate_enforce: The MTA-STS policy requires a valid TLS identity, but the certificate presented by {host} ({address}) fails the checks. Senders that apply enforce must not deliver mail to it.
mail.smtp_starttls.certificate_enforce.a: Install a certificate valid for the mail server's name
mail.smtp_starttls.certificate_invalid: The connection to {host} ({address}) can be encrypted opportunistically, but its certificate does not allow enforce to be switched on safely.
mail.smtp_starttls.certificate_invalid.a: Install a certificate valid for the mail server's name
mail.smtp_starttls.certificate_expiring: The certificate of {host} ({address}) is valid but expires in {days:day|days}: keep an eye on it.
Check the renewal of the mail server's certificate
mail.smtp_starttls.certificate_expiring_: The certificate of {host} ({address}) is still valid but expires in {days:day|days}: its renewal has probably failed.
Renew the mail server's certificate without delay
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.altered: The SMTP capabilities of {host} look altered on the network path (XXXXXXXA). Look for an ESMTP inspection in between, then compare from another network.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.smtp_refus: The server {host} refused the SMTP dialogue before STARTTLS could be checked (code 421/554 or EHLO refused). Nothing can be concluded about its TLS configuration.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.starttls_r: The server {host} announces STARTTLS but refused or deferred the command. Nothing can be concluded about its TLS configuration: check it, then check again.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.tls_versio: The TLS negotiation with {host} failed on the protocol version (TLS 1.2 and 1.3 offered). This does not prove a fault of the server: a device in between may be the cause.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.tls: The TLS negotiation with {host} did not complete. Nothing can be concluded about its TLS configuration.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.protocol: The server {host} answered outside the expected SMTP protocol. Nothing can be concluded about its TLS configuration.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.policy: The server {host} was not measured: its address is not a public address this instance may reach. This is not a fault of the server.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.no_route: The address of {host} cannot be reached from this network (no route, for example in IPv6). This does not show a fault of the server.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.network: SMTP could not be measured on {host} from this network (port 25 unreachable or too slow). This does not show a fault of the server.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.dns: The mail servers could not be discovered or resolved completely (DNS error). Nothing can be concluded.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.no_address: The mail server {host} has no published IPv4 or IPv6 address: nothing could be tested.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.invalid_na: The published mail server "{host}" is not a valid host name: it cannot be tested.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.deadline: The configured measuring time was reached. The completed observations are kept; the others were not evaluated.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.budget: The number of SMTP connections allowed per scan was reached before {host} could be concluded.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.sample: The server {host} was not part of the tested sample.
mail.smtp_starttls.unmeasured.tool: The measure of {host} could not be completed (internal error of the tool).
mail.smtp_starttls.note.untested.altered: {n:address not tested|addresses not tested} (SMTP capabilities altered): {addresses}.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.untested.smtp_re: {n:address not tested|addresses not tested} (SMTP dialogue refused): {addresses}.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.untested.starttl: {n:address not tested|addresses not tested} (STARTTLS refused or deferred): {addresses}.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.untested.tls_ver: {n:address not tested|addresses not tested} (TLS version refused): {addresses}.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.untested.protoco: {n:address not tested|addresses not tested} (reply outside the protocol): {addresses}.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.untested.policy: {n:address not tested|addresses not tested} (address not allowed by the egress rules): {addresses}.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.untested.no_rout: {n:address not tested|addresses not tested} (no route from this network): {addresses}.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.untested.network: {n:address not tested|addresses not tested} (port 25 unreachable or too slow): {addresses}.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.untested.budget: {n:address not tested|addresses not tested} (connections used up): {addresses}.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.untested.sample: {n:address not tested|addresses not tested} (outside the sample): {addresses}.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.untested.tool: {n:address not tested|addresses not tested} (error of the tool): {addresses}.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.coverage: Partial measure: {verified} of {addresses:published address verified|published addresses verified} ({mx:mail server|mail servers}). Readiness for enforce remains to be confirmed.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.sample: {n:mail server published beyond the eight tested|mail servers published beyond the eight tested}: {hosts}. Readiness for enforce cannot be confirmed on a sample.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.dns_incomplete: Incomplete DNS resolution of the mail servers: {hosts}.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.cname: The MX name {host} is an alias (CNAME to {target}), which the standard forbids (RFC 2181 §10.3). The certificate is still checked for {host}, the published name.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.verify_only: Certificate refused on {address}: only the verification error is known (no second reading of the certificate, no connection left).
mail.smtp_starttls.note.reading_interrup: Certificate refused on {address}: the second reading of the certificate was cut by the deadline; no detail is assumed.
mail.smtp_starttls.note.deadline: The configured measuring time ({seconds} s) was reached. The completed observations are kept; the others were not evaluated.
mail.smtp_starttls.readiness.title: Readiness for enforce mode
mail.smtp_starttls.readiness.ready: Ready according to the measures made from this instance
mail.smtp_starttls.readiness.compatible: Compatible with the enforce policy in force
mail.smtp_starttls.readiness.scope: This is no guarantee of delivery from the Internet: port 25 reached from this instance does not prove that other senders reach it.
mail.smtp_starttls.readiness.cause.probe: The SMTP probe is turned off on this instance.
mail.smtp_starttls.readiness.cause.inter: Internal perimeter scan: the SMTP check does not apply.
mail.smtp_starttls.readiness.cause.polic: No MTA-STS policy: first publish a policy in testing mode.
The MTA-STS policy is in none mode.
The MTA-STS policy is invalid: senders ignore it.
The MTA-STS policy file is not served.
The MTA-STS policy could not be read during this scan.
mail.smtp_starttls.readiness.cause.incom: At least one published server or address was not verified.
mail.smtp_starttls.readiness.cause.mx_cn: An MX name is an alias (CNAME): to look into before enforce.
mail.smtp_starttls.readiness.cause.start: A server does not offer STARTTLS.
mail.smtp_starttls.readiness.cause.certi: An SMTP certificate is refused (chain, name or dates).
mail.smtp_starttls.readiness.cause.mx_un: The MTA-STS policy does not cover every mail server.
mail.smtp_starttls.reason.starttls_dialo: reply to STARTTLS outside the standard
mail.smtp_starttls.starttls_message:
Hello,

The mail servers of {domain} do not offer STARTTLS on port 25: the mail they receive travels in clear. Could you turn on STARTTLS, with a certificate valid for the published name of each MX server (public chain of trust, name in the SAN)?

Thank you.
mail.smtp_starttls.certificate_message:
Hello,

At least one mail server of {domain} presents on port 25 a certificate senders cannot verify for the published MX name (public chain of trust, name in the SAN, validity dates). Could you install a certificate valid for the name of each MX, also check the backup MX and the IPv6 addresses, then read the TLS-RPT reports before switching MTA-STS to enforce?

Thank you.
mail.smtp_starttls.expiry_message:
Hello,

The certificate of at least one mail server of {domain} expires soon. Could you check its automatic renewal on each MX?

Thank you.
mail.tls_rpt.title: Encryption reports (TLS-RPT)
mail.tls_rpt.why: These daily reports list e-mails that could not reach you over an encrypted connection. They show a problem before it costs a message.
mail.tls_rpt.present: A valid TLS-RPT record advertises a reporting destination (actual report delivery is not checked).
mail.tls_rpt.how: Create the address given (or replace it with an existing one): it will get one short report per day and per sender.
mail.tls_rpt.invalid: The TLS-RPT record is invalid ({problems}): no report will be sent.
mail.tls_rpt.invalid.how: There must be a single _smtp._tls record, like "v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:address@{domain}".
mail.dmarc.testing: DMARC requests testing mode (t=y): declared policy p={policy}; receivers that follow RFC 9989 apply {effective}.
mail.dmarc.testing.action: Take DMARC out of testing mode
mail.dmarc.testing.how: With t=y, receivers that follow RFC 9989 apply the policy one level below (reject becomes quarantine, quarantine becomes none). Receivers that still follow RFC 7489 do not know t=y: they apply the declared policy, limited by "pct" when present. Once the reports show that your real e-mail passes, remove t=y.
mail.dmarc.existence_unknown: DNS could not establish whether the domain exists: the np policy inherited from {parent} cannot be assessed reliably.
mail.dmarc.invalid_monitoring: DMARC policy at {name} has an invalid policy value ({tags}): reporting-only processing may remain available.
mail.dmarc.monitoring_no_reports: DMARC is in monitoring mode (p=none) without a valid report address: fake e-mails are still delivered, and no report can show whether your real e-mail passes.
mail.dmarc.monitoring_no_reports.how: 1. In {name}, add a valid report address, as rua=mailto:address@domain, and fix the values reported. That mailbox must exist, work and be read; if it is on another domain, that domain must allow the reports with a _report._dmarc record. 2. Wait for a few days of reports and check that your real e-mail (mailbox, newsletter, invoicing) passes. 3. Only then move to p=quarantine.
mail.dmarc.partial_reject: At receivers that still follow RFC 7489, only {pct}% of the e-mails failing DMARC are selected for rejection ("pct" tag); the others should be quarantined.
mail.dmarc.note.syntax: The record {name} also has values that do not follow the standard, replaced by the defaults: {tags}.
mail.dmarc.note.partial: At receivers that still follow RFC 7489, pct={pct} also limits the quarantine to {pct}% of the failing e-mails; the others go through the usual filtering.
mail.dmarc.note.partial_reject: At receivers that still follow RFC 7489, pct={pct} also limits the rejection to {pct}% of the failing e-mails; the others should be quarantined.
mail.dmarc.note.subdomains_open: The subdomains are also left out of the policy (sp=none): a fake e-mail from invoices.{domain} would be delivered.
mail.dmarc.note.multiple_local: {name} also has several DMARC policies, which receivers ignore: the one of {parent} applies.
mail.dmarc.note.repeated: The record {name} has the same tag more than once ({tags}): the syntax of DMARC records forbids it (RFC 6376 §3.2), and some receivers may ignore the whole record.
